newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Eleven firms qualify for Guatemala electricity bid.
newsitem.headline: Eleven firms qualify for Guatemala electricity bid.

text.p: Eleven companies and consortiums have qualified to bid for two electric plants at $30 million as part of Guatemala's sweeping privatization program, a bidding consultant said on Tuesday.
"It is a very good turnout and a lot of good names," Peter A. Macaulay, executive director of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, told Reuters.

The firms are AES Americas Inc., of Arlington, Virginia.; C.A. Electricidad of Caracas; Coastal Power Co. of Houston with its subsidiary TICO; Constellation Power Development of Baltimore; Enron Caribe IV Ltd. of Houston; ENDESA Desarrollo of Spain; the consortium Energy Partners of Bethesda, Maryland; Marathon Power of Houston; Maxpower International of Marblehead, Massachusetts; ORMAT of Sparks, Nevada; and Union Fenosa of Spain.

The winning bid is scheduled to be announced on July 30. The Guatemalan Electric Company is selling off the thermoelectric plants, with a combined capacity of 80 megawatts, under the General Electricity Law which Congress passed in September.
The law demonopolizes electricity production and allows new producers to sell electricity directly to consumers on the open market.
The winning bid will offer the best package in terms of capacity and price per killowatt hour. The purchase price of $30 million has already been set.

The firms are bidding on a Power Purchase Agreement to buy 90 percent of the assets. The remaining 10 percent, valued at an additional $3 million, will be held in reserve through the end of the year to let employees secure financing to purchase shares in the new company. ((--Lorraine Orlandi, Guatemala Bureau +502 251 5718))
